title: SayMyName V1 · boucle sociale personnelle et autonome

objective.statement: SayMyName doit faire qu'au moment où la personne est en face, son nom vienne tout seul : sans écran, parmi les gens qu'on a choisi de retenir, et sans que l'effort pour y arriver se voie.

origin.statement: SayMyName is not limited to an organizational directory. Its durable purpose is to help a person recognize faces, recall names and retain chosen useful context for real-world social interactions across public culture, organizations and private life. The defensible promise is improvement on people and information actually trained, not broad intelligence, health or therapeutic claims.

conflicts.summary: LeaderboardDao.getTop()/findTop() and LeaderboardController (/api/leaderboard, /api/leaderboard/me) return every user's displayName, XP, rank and lastAnswerAt with no tenant/organization scoping, to any authenticated user — contradicting the private-learning criterion's acceptance that no organization admin can observe an individual learner's progress.

code_evidence.ref: rigs/saymyname-backend/persistence/src/main/java/com/saymyname/persistence/dao/leaderboard/LeaderboardDao.java — getTop()/findTop() has no tenant/user-scoping predicate; returns every user's stat row platform-wide

rigs/saymyname-backend/webapp/src/main/java/com/saymyname/webapp/controller/LeaderboardController.java — GET /api/leaderboard and /api/leaderboard/me require only an authenticated Principal, no organization-membership check

conflicts.intent_ref: criteria/private-learning acceptance: «Un administrateur d’organisation connecté au même environnement ne peut observer ni les sélections, ni les erreurs, ni le planning, ni la progression individuelle d’un apprenant.»
conflicts.resolution_detail: Benjamin 2026-09-18: redesign entirely, competitive like Duolingo, compare only what is comparable; scope delegated to the PO. The global board is removed; boards are per collection inside one audience (public collection, or one organization), weekly, opt-in per learner, exposing display name + weekly XP + rank only, with no administrator view. See DECISIONS.md 2026-09-18.

findings.summary: Frontend router/feature folders and backend HTTP controllers scanned 2026-09-14 found existing surfaces for access (sign in/up, verification, recovery), invitation/onboarding, learning (training, course, quiz, progress), people (trombinoscope, profile, search, subscriptions) and organization admin (dashboard, people, members, invitations, attributes, change requests); no complete public-challenge, personal-home or CSV-import customer journey existed yet at that date.

The same scan lists authentication/session/recovery, invitations and scoped organization administration, person/profile data with photos/attributes/subscriptions/search primitives, and a full quiz/course lifecycle (answers, help, statistics, performance, leaderboard) as already present before any Factory-delivered SayMyName work.

Durable product documentation set located by header scan and read end to end for this migration: OBJECTIVE.md, DECISIONS.md, PRODUCT_STRATEGY.md, PRODUCT_CONTEXT.md, DESIGN_GOVERNANCE.md, EXPOSURE_REVIEW.md, PO_WORKSPACE_AGENTS.md and PROJECT_INVENTORY.md.

Beads/GitHub history since the 2026-09-14 scan shows af-u8id.2 (personal-home/groups foundation), af-u8id.3 plus af-u8id.3.1 (administered CSV, backend PR #38 and frontend PR #49) and af-ccvr (personal CSV) as Factory-delivered work built on top of the pre-existing surfaces above, not discovered code — those capabilities are therefore not takeover-derived even though some reuse takeover-derived primitives underneath.

questions.prompt: What does "done" mean for SayMyName V1 — which increments are in scope and which are evidence-gated extensions?
questions.answer: V1 is the public-challenge + personal-home foundation, the participative promotion/event journey, the France-first French-presidents collection, administered-organization CSV import, personal people import and the scoped editorial publication workflow; natural-language retrieval, the first external connector, federation, pricing and general launch readiness remain evidence-gated extensions outside the V1 completion contract.

questions.prompt: How is personal data exposed, and what consent governs group visibility, retention and continuity?
questions.answer: Groups are private by default with no profile exposed in a join preview; a claimed profile has an account-wide sharing default plus a granular, reversible per-group choice; personal continuity is an explicit authorized copy, never a silent export, and revocation removes copied fields; an unclaimed organization-imported profile is not personally copyable after access ends.

questions.prompt: What production-data, migration or publication actions are irreversible, and how are they bounded?
questions.answer: Agent database inspection is read-only; Flyway owns schema migrations and persistent migration execution needs explicit authorization; tests use isolated, ephemeral databases only.

questions.prompt: What pricing, spend or contractual-commitment decisions apply to V1?
questions.answer: Payment stays outside the V1 boundary, and every Enterprise-tier decision (pilot recruitment, tester pool, pricing/buyer identity, brand/name) is retracted and deferred until after V1 release; no Enterprise-tier question is raised, decided or acted on before then.

questions.prompt: Who owns the product and who may approve on the human's behalf?
questions.answer: The PO owns what and why — product intent, priority, acceptance, durable context and the concise conversation with Benjamin; the Mayor owns how and execution — Beads, formulas, dispatch, PR/CI/merge and operational closure; once an outcome is handed off the PO never runs a parallel control loop over the Mayor.

questions.prompt: What licensing, regulatory or contractual constraints govern published content?
questions.answer: Public cultural challenges require versioned editorial review, factual and image provenance, license/rights handling and withdrawal; anonymous trial is allowed but saving progress requires an account, and editorial roles stay scoped to the public catalogue rather than an omnipotent super-admin.

persistence/dao/leaderboard/LeaderboardDao.java getTop()/findTop() and webapp/controller/LeaderboardController.java (/api/leaderboard, /api/leaderboard/me): no tenant/organization scoping predicate — see origin.conflicts.leaderboard-cross-org-exposure

review.notes: Tier 1 static: person-directory attribute-guard and SRS/course-selection unit tests pass on both rigs, CI green on both rigs' dev tip, /code-review at effort low surfaced no findings on the cited paths. Reserved class (identity_and_consent: exposure of personal data) escalates to tier 2 regardless. Tier 2 (model-assisted): the private-learning criterion's own acceptance — no organization admin can observe an individual learner's selections, errors, schedule or progress — is contradicted by the pre-existing, takeover-derived global leaderboard: LeaderboardDao.getTop()/findTop() carries no tenant/organization predicate and LeaderboardController's /api/leaderboard and /api/leaderboard/me endpoints require only an authenticated Principal, exposing every user's XP, rank and lastAnswerAt (a direct proxy for individual progress) to any authenticated user regardless of organization. The admin-facing person-directory DTOs do not themselves leak progress, so the gap is specifically the pre-existing leaderboard, not the new private-selection layer. Verdict: needs_rework. Recorded as origin.conflicts.leaderboard-cross-org-exposure with reserved outcome decision leaderboard-exposure-outcome (keep_target/adapt_target/mix) — the choice itself is not made here, per ADR-0015 §5b; a keep_target fix (tenant-scope the leaderboard) is offered as the recommendation, not the decision. Follow-up work tracked as product-queue candidate af-9qn1q under af-u8id.

criteria.title: Choix et apprentissage privés
criteria.description: Aucune organisation ne voit les sélections, erreurs, réponses, planning ou progression individuelle.
criteria.acceptance: Un administrateur d’organisation connecté au même environnement ne peut observer ni les sélections, ni les erreurs, ni le planning, ni la progression individuelle d’un apprenant. Seule exception : un apprenant qui a explicitement rejoint un classement y expose son nom affiché, son XP de la semaine et son rang, sur ce seul classement (une collection dans une audience), sans vue administrateur dédiée ; un apprenant qui ne l’a pas rejoint reste invisible de tous.
